=== PUC Comments on 58481 2nd Round of Comments.pdf ===
                                       PROJECT NO. 58481



 RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                         §     PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                      §
 STANDARDS UNDER PURA § 37.0561                  §                     OF TEXAS




       CIPHER DIGITAL COMMENTS TO STAFF PROPOSED PROPOSAL FOR
                            PUBLICATION
       Cipher Digital Inc. appreciates the opportunity to comment on Project No. 58481,
Rulemaking Relating to the Implementation of Senate Bill 6 (89R) and PURA § 37.0561 (the
“Project”) and respectfully submits this 2nd comment letter for consideration.

        Cipher supports the Commission’s decision to reduce the financial security and
interconnection fee commitments from $100,000 per megawatt (MW) to $50,000 per MW on March
12, 2026, following Chairman Gleeson’s memorandum, dated March 11, 2026, which recommends a
$50,000 per MW non-refundable interconnection fee. This fee, while burdensome for us and other
large load developers, is in the range that satisfies the Legislature’s intent in SB 6 to ensure large
loads pay for transmission upgrades.

        Cipher would like to propose what it views as a necessary clarification. In the event that the
Independent Organization (ERCOT) re-allocates load in a batch study, the MWs that are re-allocated
should be refunded to the large load customer. For example, if a load is requesting 500 MWs and
ERCOT allocates 300 MWs to that load during the batch process, then the $50,000 per MW for the
200 MWs that were re-allocated should be refunded to the large load customer. Consider adding this
sentence to the proposal for publication: In the event that the Independent Organization re-allocates
load from the large load customer, the TSP shall refund the $50,000 per MW interconnection fee to
the large load customer for the MWs that were re-allocated.

       To clarify, this is not meant to capture a situation where the large load customer opted to
remove itself but rather a situation where ERCOT was not able to serve the entire load. We greatly
appreciate the Commission’s attention to this important detail.

Respectfully submitted,


Lee Bratcher
Head of Policy and Government Affairs
Cipher Digital
lee.bratcher@cipherdigital.com
                                   Executive Summary


         In the event that the Independent Organization (ERCOT) re-allocates load in a batch
study, the MWs that are re-allocated should be refunded to the large load customer. For example,
if a load is requesting 500 MWs and ERCOT allocates 300 MWs to that load during the batch
process, then the $50,000 per MW for the 200 MWs that were re-allocated should be refunded to
the large load customer.
